ties.applies_to: a tie vote between candidates at a primary or general election in state or district elections, canvassed by the state board of canvassers and the secretary of state
ties.steps: the interested parties or their authorized agents appear before the secretary of state within two days after the canvass, and the tie is determined by a toss of a coin

sources.quote: In the case of a tie vote between the candidates at a primary or general election, the interested parties or their authorized agents shall appear before the secretary of state within two (2) days after the canvass and the tie shall be determined by a toss of a coin.

ties.note: The section's heading says 'in state or district elections' and its text says 'a primary or general election'; it is read as covering state offices, state legislative (district) offices and federal offices, whose certificates the secretary of state issues with state and district offices (34-1215, in chapter 12 as read) [inferred for federal offices]. Chapters 12 (canvass of votes) and 23 (recount) were read; no section for a tie after a recount was found.

ties.applies_to: a tie vote between candidates at a primary or general election in county elections
ties.steps: the interested candidates appear before the county clerk within two days after the canvass, and the tie is determined by a toss of a coin

sources.quote: In the case of a tie vote between candidates at a primary election or general election, the interested candidates shall appear before the county clerk within two (2) days after the canvass and the tie shall be determined by a toss of a coin.

ties.note: Title 34 chapter 12; applies to county offices. Municipal, school and special-district elections are run under other titles of the Idaho Code (not read), so they are not recorded as covered; charters and ordinances were not read.

ties.steps: read through the general rule for state elections: a toss of a coin before the secretary of state

sources.quote: In the case of a tie vote between the candidates at a primary or general election, the interested parties or their authorized agents shall appear before the secretary of state within two (2) days after the canvass and the tie shall be determined by a toss of a coin.

ties.note: No section of chapters 12 or 23 names presidential electors; the reading that 34-1216 reaches a tie among them is the reader's [inferred]. The chapter on presidential electors was not read.

ties.applies_to: a ballot measure that ends tied
ties.note: Read: Title 34 chapters 12 (canvass of votes, whole chapter PDF) and 23 (recount of ballots, whole chapter PDF). Both tie sections (34-1210, 34-1216) speak of candidates only. Chapter 23 applies its recount rules to measures. Other chapters of Title 34 (for example on ballot questions) and the Constitution were not read.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for that office
threshold.conditions: for a measure, the difference between the yes and no votes; request in writing, filed with the appropriate officer within twenty days of the canvass (34-2301)
threshold.in_words: a margin less than or equal to one-tenth of one percent of the votes cast for the office, or five votes, whichever is greater

who_may_request: a losing candidate for nomination or election
a person supporting or opposing a ballot measure
recounts.cost_bearer: the state for a federal, state or legislative district office or a state measure; the county for a county, city or district office or measure

sources.quote: A losing candidate for nomination, or election or person supporting or opposing a ballot measure, may request a recount of the votes cast for the nomination or election to that office or passage or failure of a measure if the difference between the vote cast for that candidate and for the winning candidate for nomination or election, or the difference between the yes and no votes on a measure, is less than or equal to one-tenth of one percent (0.1%) of the total votes cast for that office or five (5) votes, whichever is greater.
The state shall pay for the recount of a federal, state, or legislative district office, or state measure while the county shall pay for the recount of a county, city or district office or measure.

recounts.note: Called the 'free recount' in the section's heading. It is on request, not automatic: no recount happens in Idaho without a request in the sections read. For a measure the text compares yes and no votes with '0.1% of the total votes cast for that office or five votes', so the percentage's base for a measure is not stated [as written].

threshold.conditions: application within twenty days of the canvass: to the attorney general for federal, state, county or municipal office or a state, county or city measure; to the county clerk for all other offices and measures; the requester states the precincts and remits $100 for each; to be relieved of costs the requester must ask for at least 20 precincts with 5,000 votes (federal or state office or measure), 5 precincts with 1,250 votes (state legislative district), 2 precincts with 500 votes (county office or measure), or 2 precincts with 200 votes (city or district elections)
threshold.in_words: any candidate for federal, state, county or municipal office, or any person supporting or opposing a measure, may apply for a recount of chosen precincts at $100 a precinct, whatever the margin

who_may_request: any candidate for federal, state, county or municipal office desiring a recount
a person supporting or opposing a state, county or city measure
candidates for all other offices and supporters and opponents of all other measures (to the county clerk)
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester ($100 per precinct), unless the recount shows a difference that, projected across all the precincts of the office, would change the result in the requester's favor: then the county or state bears the cost, the money is returned, and a general recount of the remaining precincts is required (34-2307, in the chapter PDF)

sources.quote: Any candidate for federal, state, county or municipal office desiring a recount of the ballots cast in any nominating or general election or person supporting or opposing a state, county or city measure, may apply to the attorney general therefor, within twenty (20) days of the canvass of such election
the sum of one hundred dollars ($100) for each such precinct in which he desires a recount made.

If the results of the recount indicate a difference, which if projected across all the precincts of the office in question would change the result of the election in favor of the candidate requesting the recount or change in the measure being recounted, then the cost of such recount shall be borne by the county or state
shall require a recount to be made in all the remaining precincts of the office in question.

recounts.note: No margin condition is stated in 34-2301 or 34-2302 [as written]; the rule is read as available whatever the margin, at the requester's cost, and the cost is refunded if the recount shows a result-changing difference.

unread.what: municipal, school-district and other special-district elections (other titles of the Idaho Code), the chapter on presidential electors, and any provision on ballot-question ties
unread.reason: not read; outside Title 34 chapters 12 and 23, which are the canvass and the recount chapters

notes: Idaho was read at the Idaho Legislature's site: the Title 34 contents page, the two chapter pages, the whole-chapter PDFs of chapters 12 and 23 (a documented download linked from each chapter page), and five section pages. The PDFs break words with hyphens at line ends, so quotations are taken from the section pages except 34-2302, whose quoted words are not broken.
Idaho has no automatic recount in the sections read; every recount is on request. Ties are settled by a toss of a coin.
